calls.reason: Largely rhetorical. The OpenClaw FAQ makes a Mac mini optional, and the PinchBench v1 scores look strong, but the benchmark's operator later disclosed grading flaws. No matched cost or reliability comparison exists.
A broad causal opinion. The test-time scaling and tiny-recursive-model papers don't isolate what constrains progress across the industry, so the evidence can't settle it.

NVIDIA's release supports the ~90% data center share (89.7%). The 8% index weight is unverified, and no buyer-level evidence shows immediate losses; AWS's positive operating income cuts the other way.
Sightline's 5GW covers only projects due to open in 2026. JLL reports a 35GW North American construction pipeline, with Texas alone at 6.5GW under construction, far above 5GW overall.

Hedged wording, and the company group is undefined. The only counterexample offered, Cursor's $2B annualized rate in March 2026, isn't realized 2025 revenue, so the 'only' claim is neither confirmed nor refuted.

Anthropic's audited S-1 shows a $42B net loss in 2025 (about $7.7B excluding fair-value charges), and reporting puts OpenAI near $39B ($8B ex-charge). Both lost billions; the hedged margin point is secondary.
